rows.question: Within exactly how many days is a refund processed?

hits.title: Subscription cancellation and refund policy
hits.text: Northstar Labs customers may request a refund within 7 days of their first paid subscription if fewer than 100 research queries have been used. Renewals are non-refundable. Cancelling disables the next renewal while access remains available until the paid period ends. Refund requests are reviewed by billing support. This policy does not specify the number of days required to process a refund.

hits.title: Data retention schedule
hits.text: Northstar Labs retains application audit logs for 90 days. Billing records are retained for 7 years. Customer-uploaded research documents are retained until the customer deletes them. Deleted documents are removed from active storage within 24 hours and age out of encrypted backups within 30 days. Legal holds can suspend the normal deletion schedule.

hits.title: Incident response procedure
hits.text: At Northstar Labs a SEV-1 incident must be acknowledged within 10 minutes. The incident commander posts customer-facing updates every 30 minutes until resolution. A written incident review is due within 3 business days after resolution. A SEV-2 incident has a 30-minute acknowledgement target. Incident reviews focus on contributing systems rather than blame.

hits.title: Public API usage limits
hits.text: Northstar Labs public API allows 120 requests per minute per API key. Requests above this limit return HTTP 429 with a Retry-After header. Clients should respect Retry-After and use exponential backoff with jitter. Idempotency keys are retained for 24 hours and apply only to POST /jobs. The API does not promise exactly-once delivery of webhooks.

hits.title: Webhook delivery behavior
hits.text: Northstar Labs retries failed webhook deliveries at most 3 times over 15 minutes. Receivers must deduplicate by event_id because a delivery can be repeated. An HTTP 2xx response counts as endpoint acceptance, not downstream job completion. Webhook signing secrets can be rotated in account settings. Retries stop when the subscription is disabled.

hits.title: Backup and recovery procedure
hits.text: Northstar Labs takes encrypted database backups every 6 hours and retains backups for 30 days. Recovery point objective is 6 hours; recovery time objective is 4 hours. A restore drill is performed once per quarter. The on-call database engineer owns restore execution. Backup success alone is not evidence that a restore will work.

hits.title: Workspace access roles
hits.text: At Northstar Labs, administrators manage user accounts and shared settings. Members create and approve their own research tasks. Viewers may read their own history but cannot create or approve tasks. Administrators do not automatically gain access to another user's private research. Disabling an account revokes active sessions.

hits.title: Research retrieval architecture
hits.text: Northstar Labs document search uses 1,200-character passages with 180-character overlap. Keyword retrieval uses BM25. Hybrid retrieval fuses BM25 and dense cosine-similarity rankings with reciprocal rank fusion and a rank constant of 60. Retrieval returns at most 4 passages by default. A matching passage is a candidate source, not proof that a generated claim is correct.

hits.title: Remote work policy
hits.text: Northstar Labs permits remote work up to 3 days per week. Team members must be reachable during core hours of 11:00 to 15:00 UTC. Working from another country requires written People Operations approval before travel. The policy provides no list of permitted countries. Remote equipment purchases follow the equipment policy, not the travel policy.

rows.question: What accuracy does Northstar guarantee on real customer research questions?

hits.title: AI evaluation protocol
hits.text: Northstar Labs keeps development and test questions separate. Prompt selection uses only the development split. Retrieval is evaluated with recall at k and reciprocal rank. Generated answers are audited for factual correctness, citation support, appropriate abstention, latency and token usage. Test-set results must include failures, not only successful examples. No production accuracy claim can be inferred from this fictional policy benchmark.
